answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a real wind turbine on a named ridge. A certified technician climbs the tower during a gale, reads the turbine control kernel's serial number, and bolts a tamper-evident anchor seal to the nacelle. Random spot-checks summon the holder to climb that exact turbine within a day, and one climber cannot service two turbines in the same storm. The certification fee, paid in outside money, doubles for each further turbine on the same funding trail, so every extra fake identity costs another real climb, another live technician, and twice the prior fee.
